q: I recorded a 20-minute talking-head video; what's a good basic edit?
a: 1. Transcribe and remove long pauses and filler words (`transcript.removePauses`, `transcript.removeFillers`), then watch it through and put back pauses where thoughts end. 2. Punch in on alternate cuts (Motion Scale 110–120 %) to soften jumps. 3. Clean Up Voice on the audio (`audio.cleanupVoice`). 4. Simple balance and skin check. 5. Captions from the transcript and chapters from markers. Options: cut tighter for YouTube energy, leave more air for a calm explainer.

q: talking head looks boring, how do I keep people watching
a: Change the picture every few seconds in long stretches: punch-ins (100 % / 115 %), B-roll on V2 over the voice, a lower third or a callout, an occasional graphic. Vary the device; constant zooms tire people.

q: Talking head shot against a window, face too dark and the window blown.
a: A soft tracked ellipse window on the face with Gamma up, a curve shoulder / soft clip for the window (clipped areas stay white); expose for the face next time or add light.

q: How do I edit a comedy sketch so the jokes land?
a: Timing is in the pauses: leave a beat before the punchline and cut to the reaction a moment after it (an L-cut keeps the line's audio while you show the reaction). Cut long first and tighten in passes, watching in real time. Remove dead air between lines, but not the beat before the laugh.

q: awkward silence joke, how long do I hold
a: Hold longer than feels comfortable on the awkward shot, then cut on a small action (a blink, a sip) or a sound; trim frame by frame with a rolling edit until it plays right in real time.

q: Add a comedic record-scratch stop and a zoom on the reaction.
a: Cut at the moment, a quick Scale push on the reactor's face (Hold interpolation for a snap), a record-scratch sound on an SFX track, and duck or cut the music there.

q: Moody fashion film with slow motion and a strobe feel.
a: Slow motion from high-frame-rate footage (Speed / Duration so every frame shows), a contrasty, slightly desaturated look node, and the strobe: Strobe Light (Video Effects ▸ Stylize) or Posterize Time on some shots, cut to the music's beats. Keep flashing short and gentle.

q: make the clothes' colours pop but skin stay natural
a: Qualify the garment colours on their own node and raise saturation there; protect skin with a skin qualifier node (or limit with windows) so faces stay on the skin line.

q: Elegant titles for a fashion film.
a: One thin, wide typeface, small sizes, lots of space; titles centred or aligned to the frame (graphics.arrange), slow eased fades; check legibility over moving footage (thin fonts can flicker after compression).

q: A short explainer video for my app with icons and text.
a: 1. Write the script; a text-to-speech draft (`tts.create`) gives timing before recording the real voice. 2. Screen recordings in a sequence at their size, zooms with eased Scale keyframes. 3. Icons and labels as shape and text layers, saved as templates with only the text editable. 4. Music typed Music with Ducking under the voice. 5. Captions from the transcript.

q: animated bullet points appearing one by one
a: One text layer (or graphic) per bullet, each starting a little later on the timeline, sliding in with eased Position and Opacity keyframes; a template for the bullet style keeps them identical.

q: Explainer voice-over: record myself or AI voice?
a: Text to speech for drafts, explainers on a budget and late line changes (sounds synthetic, little emphasis control); your own recording for personality (needs a quiet room; Takes make re-recording easy). Many do both: draft with TTS, record over the same timing.

q: Datamosh effect where one shot melts into the next.
a: Revolution has no datamosh (codec-smearing) effect. Approximations: the Glitch shader or Glitch transition at the cut, Turbulent Displace keyframed up across the edit, or Echo for smearing motion. A real datamosh needs a tool that edits the compressed stream, made elsewhere and imported.

q: pixel melting glitch on the beat
a: Turbulent Displace with its amount keyframed up on beat markers, plus Glitch shader bursts; GPU-only for the shader.

q: Datamosh on a whole music video, consistent.
a: Build the look on an Adjustment Layer above the sequence (Turbulent Displace / Glitch with keyframes on the hits), so one set of settings covers every clip.

q: Time-slice effect: vertical strips of the same shot from different moments.
a: Locked-off timelapse or long shot. Stack several copies of the clip on tracks, each starting at a different time (slip them), each with a rectangle mask on Opacity covering one vertical strip (`masks.add`). Together the strips show the scene changing across the frame (sunrise to night in slices).

q: time slice strips should have soft edges
a: Raise each strip mask's Feather so neighbouring times blend; align the strips with Mask Expansion so no gaps show.

q: Time slice in a comp to manage 10 strips.
a: Ten Media In nodes reading the clip at different offsets, each through a Mask node with its strip, merged in a chain → Media Out; the graph keeps the strips readable.

q: How do I use reaction shots of the interviewer to cover edits?
a: Record noddies (listening reactions) after the interview. In the edit, put a noddy on V2 over a cut in the answer, video only (target V2, source audio off, `timeline.setTargeting`), while the answer's audio carries on. Keep them short and natural.

q: two-camera interview: cut to the listener while the guest talks
a: In the multicam, switch to the listener's angle for a moment while the guest's audio continues (turn audio-follows-video off so the sound stays on the guest's source); a cut on a natural reaction looks best.

q: Noddy shots look obviously fake.
a: Use real listening moments from the conversation rather than staged nods, keep them under two seconds, and match their grade to the main camera.

q: Nature documentary feel for my wildlife footage.
a: Natural grade (balance and contrast, no heavy look), slow motion on key behaviour (Speed / Duration), long ambience beds of the location under everything, a calm narration (record it, Clean Up Voice) with music ducked under it, and patient pacing.

q: telephoto wildlife shots are shaky and hazy
a: Warp Stabilizer (Smooth Motion) for long-lens shake; for haze, a little more contrast and saturation on the subject (a soft window), black point set on the waveform.

q: Nature doc narration voice with a deep, warm tone.
a: Clean Up Voice first, then Clarity ▸ EQ with the Warm Voice preset and gentle Dynamics; keep the music well under it.

q: Cinemagraph: everything frozen except the steam rising from the coffee.
a: Locked-off shot. A Frame Hold of the clip on V2 (`clip.frameHold`) over the live clip on V1, with a mask on the hold's Opacity around the steam area, Inverted and feathered, so only the steam moves. Loop it seamlessly (a dissolve from its end into its start).

q: cinemagraph loop has a jump at the restart
a: Overlap the end onto the start with a Cross Dissolve, or pick a loop length where the moving part matches; for steam or water, a dissolve hides it well.

q: Export a cinemagraph for Instagram.
a: Repeat the loop a few times on the timeline, export as H.264 MP4 at the platform's size (a 4:5 or 9:16 sequence), short and silent or with ambience.

q: Save-the-date video for our wedding with photos and our names.
a: Photos with slow eased Scale moves, soft dissolves, a gentle song fitted with Remix, and an elegant title template with names and date editable (`graphics.template.apply`); end on the date card held long enough to read.

q: warm romantic grade on the save the date clips
a: Gain slightly warm, soft contrast, lifted blacks a touch, Wonder Glow with a low intensity on the highlights; copy the look node to all clips (`grade.append`).

q: Vertical and square versions of the save the date.
a: Duplicate the sequence (`edit.duplicate`) at 1080 × 1920 and 1080 × 1080, reposition clips (or Auto Reframe), move the titles into the new frames, and queue all exports.
